- When sentiment is low (≤0.3) or shows strong negative momentum, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above recent peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.7) and price is rising, model frequently overreacts; apply downward bias of 1–2% to forecast if sentiment >0.7 and price >65.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is weak but price is trending up; if sentiment <0.4 and price >60, add 0.5–1.5% to forecast.
- Forecast tends to lag by 1–2 days in upward trends; if true price rises >1% from prior day, adjust forecast up by 0.5–1.5% for next day.
- When sentiment is volatile (fluctuating >0.25) and price is near 65–70, model often overcorrects; apply smoothing: average last 3 forecast values before adjusting.
- If sentiment is consistently low (≤0.2) over 3+ days, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to account for mean reversion toward higher levels.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates near end of period; reduce final 3–5 forecast values by 0.5–1.5% if sentiment is weak or flat.
